common.fallbackNotice: Albanian is not populated yet — showing English.

auth.noAccessTitle: This account has no access to MG2030
auth.noAccessBody: You are signed in, but this account is not registered on the MG2030 platform. It may belong to another application hosted on the same infrastructure. If you believe this is a mistake, contact the project coordinator.
auth.pendingBody: Your MG2030 account exists but has not been activated yet. An administrator must approve it before you can see project data.
auth.requestMessageHint: Say which sub-project or contract you work on. It saves an exchange.
auth.requestSent: Your request has been sent. The administrators have been notified by email.
auth.signUpNotice: Creating an account does NOT give you access to the data. It is not a member of the project until an administrator assigns it an organisation, a role and a scope. You will land on a waiting screen.
auth.confirmEmailNotice: Account created. Confirm your address from the email we sent, then sign in — you will be able to request access from the waiting screen.
auth.awaitingBody: Your request has been recorded and the administrators have been notified. Your account carries no access to project data until one of them assigns it an organisation, a role and a scope. To follow it up, contact {admins}.
auth.rejectedBody: Your request was reviewed and not granted. If you believe this is a mistake, contact {admins}.
auth.error_shortPassword: The password must be at least {min} characters.
auth.error_alreadyMember: This account is already a member of the project.
auth.error_writeFailed: The request could not be recorded.
auth.existingAccount: This email address already has an account in the project. Supabase does not send a confirmation email in that case — creating a new one is not possible. Sign in with your existing password instead; if you don't have access to MG2030 yet, the next screen will let you request it.
auth.forgotPasswordIntro: Enter the email address of your account. If it exists, we'll send a link to set a new password.
auth.resetLinkSent: If that address has an account, a reset link is on its way. Check your inbox — the link expires after a while, so use it soon.
auth.error_passwordMismatch: The two passwords do not match.

errors.generic: Something went wrong. Please try again.

demo.title: Design system
demo.intro: Every primitive of the MG2030 interface, in each of its states. This page exists so the charter can be reviewed without opening a feature screen.
demo.tokensIntro: Single source: lib/tokens.ts. No colour is written by hand anywhere else.
demo.brandPalette: Institutional palette — emblem of the Republic of Kosovo
demo.accent2Note: Emblem border and map of Kosovo
demo.buttonsIntro: Four variants. The accent carries the primary action; --danger is reserved for destructive ones.
demo.loadingNote: The label is replaced and the button becomes disabled. No spinner.
demo.fieldsIntro: Focus ring in forms, border only in table cells. The field-level error style did not exist in the charter repository: it is added here.
demo.fieldErrorHint: Leaving the field empty triggers the error.
demo.cellNote: A ring would spill over neighbouring cells, so only the border is used.
demo.containersIntro: A surface sitting in the flow has no shadow, only a border. Shadows are reserved for what floats above.
demo.cardNote: Everyday container: framed table, panel, page block. 8 px radius, 1 px border, no shadow.
demo.panelNote: Full-page card: sign-in, access-denied screen. 12 px radius, 32 px padding, light shadow.
demo.okNoteLong: Positive action — never the accent, which would read as a signal
demo.statusesIntro: Pastel palette taken from the charter repository. The « late » red is deliberately mild and distinct from --danger.
demo.tablesIntro: List table, light header. The dark-header summary table and the editable grid ship with the modules that use them.
demo.formatsIntro: Dates as dd/mm/yyyy in both languages, amounts in euros excluding tax, durations in calendar days.
demo.planDateWhy: Calendar day, no time zone: no risk of a one-day shift
demo.amountWhy: The « excl. VAT » suffix prevents reading tax-inclusive figures where the seed is tax-exclusive
demo.rangeWhy: Works lots carry bounds, not a single value
demo.missingWhy: Never 0 nor an empty string: missing data must be visible
demo.i18nIntro: No hard-coded string, from the very first component (brief §6).
demo.fallbackExplain: Albanian is out of scope for version 1 (brief §9): the infrastructure is ready, the dictionary is still to be validated by the PIU. Any missing key falls back to English — that is the expected behaviour, not a failure.

home.stateIntro: The consolidated dashboard is out of scope for version 1 (brief §9). These are the figures worth opening the platform for — each one leads to its screen.
home.unownedNote: {count} tasks carry no owner, so no lateness alert has a recipient (GAPS 8). The source spreadsheet contained none — and only one account exists so far, so there is barely anyone to assign to yet.

users.title: Users
users.intro: Around 30 accounts, all internal, created by invitation. There is no self sign-up (brief §3).
users.name: Name
users.sharedAuthWarning: Warning — the authentication pool is shared with another application on the same Supabase project. Being signed in does not grant access to MG2030: only a row in this table does.
users.cannotDeactivateSelf: You cannot deactivate your own account.
users.roleHint: Only roles of organisation {org} are offered: a role from another organisation would grant permissions designed for a different line of work.
users.scopeReplacedNote: The scope is REPLACED, not added to. A user carries one scope, not a collection of forgotten ones.
users.error_targetRequired: Choose what the scope applies to.
users.requestsIntro: People who created an account and are waiting to be assigned. Until then they see a waiting screen and read no project data — RLS grants nothing to a non-member.
users.approveHint: Creates the member account with this organisation and role.
users.approveNote: The account is created INACTIVE and with no scope: activate it and set its scope from the accounts table below. An approved account is not yet a configured account.
users.error_alreadyHandled: This request has already been handled.

sites.title: Sites
sites.intro: 14 sites in Prishtina: the Student Center and 13 physical education halls.
sites.name: Name
sites.missingGeo: Addresses and GPS coordinates are absent from every source document. They are not omitted here — they do not exist yet (GAPS 1 and 2), and the map module needs them.
sites.error_latLonTogether: Latitude and longitude go together — fill both or neither.

buildings.title: Buildings
buildings.intro: 36 buildings: 23 at the Student Center, 13 training venue halls.
buildings.name: Name
buildings.zoneNote: Zone applies to the Student Center only. The 13 training venue halls have none.
buildings.areaNote: Where net and gross areas differ markedly, both come from the sources and neither has been arbitrated (GAPS 17).
buildings.error_missingFields: Code, name and site are required.

contracts.title: Contracts
contracts.intro: Contracts with their lots nested underneath. Filters combine, and a contract kept brings its lots with it. Free text also searches the lots: looking for a lot name brings back the contract that holds it.
contracts.name: Name
contracts.notApplicableDirect: Not applicable — direct contracting, so no notice is published
contracts.numberNote: The XX suffix is not yet assigned, so contract numbers are not unique. The functional key is the contract code (GAPS 19).
contracts.estimateNote: 8 of the 9 contracts are marked TBD in the procurement plan (GAPS 5).
contracts.numberFormatHint: Format: MYS/MG2030/{C|W|G|NC|DB}/{year}/XX. XX is accepted literally — the real suffix is not yet assigned.

lots.title: Lots
lots.name: Name
lots.unassignedNote: The split of the 13 training venue halls across the 4 works lots is not settled (GAPS 3). An unknown assignment is an absence of data, not an empty lot.
lots.error_minAboveMax: The minimum amount cannot be greater than the maximum.
lots.unassignedSummary: {count} lots have no buildings assigned yet. Their composition is not settled — it is not a count of zero (GAPS 3).
lots.sameContractWarning: {count} of these buildings already belong to another lot of the SAME contract. That usually means the same works counted twice — but it is your call, not a rule, so nothing is blocked.
lots.alreadyInHint: Already assigned to this other lot of the same contract.
lots.searchBuildings: Search a building or a site…

schedule.title: Plan
schedule.intro: The editable grid and the Gantt are one page: the diagram is the continuation of the columns, not a second view to keep in sync. Durations are in calendar days; weeks = days / 7.
schedule.keyboardHint: Click or tab into a cell to edit. Enter validates and moves down, Tab validates and moves right, Escape cancels. Ctrl+Z undoes, Ctrl+Y redoes. Drag a row by its body to reorder it within its group, or use the arrows. There is no save button: validating a cell writes it and recalculates the downstream chain.
schedule.noPlanTooltip: No usable schedule for this scenario
schedule.driftNote: A gold dot marks a task whose stored dates differ from the recalculated ones. After the GAPS 12 correction the two coincide, so a drift means either an unsaved change or data touched outside the application.
schedule.driverProjectStart: Falls back to the project start date
schedule.invalidDuration: Duration must be a whole number of days, zero or more.
schedule.unschedulableBody: This scenario is loaded without any task, on purpose. The source spreadsheet computes it backwards from the end of the Design & Build route, which puts works completion in October 2031, 21 months after the Games. No date has been invented to fill the gap (brief §7).
schedule.unschedulableFix: The procurement plan does contain a coherent timeline for this route: works from 27/03/2027 to 12/09/2029. What is missing is only the breakdown into tasks, which the PIU or the technical assistance can produce. See docs/GAPS.md, point 9.
schedule.predecessorsHint: Row numbers, comma-separated — 3, 7. Finish-to-start: this task begins the day its latest predecessor ends, and follows it automatically. Setting a predecessor releases any pinned start date, otherwise the link would have no effect. Empty detaches the task and frees its start again.
schedule.unassignedNote: {count} task(s) have no owner. Lateness notifications have no recipient until one is set — the source spreadsheet contained none (GAPS 8).
schedule.typeHint_summary: Dates are aggregated from its children — you do not set them.
schedule.typeHint_group_header: Organises the list. Carries no date, and does NOT aggregate its children.
schedule.durationHint: Calendar days, not working days. Weeks = days / 7, as in the source file.
schedule.createNote: The new task is added at the end of the list, with no predecessor: it falls back to the project start date until you link it. Set its predecessors in the grid to place it in the chain.
schedule.scenarioNotSchedulable: This scenario has no usable schedule: adding a task would mean inventing dates, which the brief forbids.
schedule.filteredNote: Filtered view: {shown} of {total} rows. Row numbers keep their value across views, so predecessors stay meaningful. Parent rows are kept so the indentation still reads, and a dependency with one end hidden draws no arrow.
schedule.contractHint: Which contract funds this task. Drives the contract filter and the procurement view.
schedule.rowNoHint: Row number, renumbered automatically. This is what you type in the Predecessors column — hover a number to see its WBS code.
schedule.predecessorsFormHint: Predecessors are entered in the grid, in the Predecessors column: row numbers separated by commas.
schedule.startDrivenBy: Driven by row {rows}: finish-to-start. The start is a result, not an entry. To hold this task back further, use « Not before » below.
schedule.cycleNotice: A precedence cycle makes the schedule impossible to compute. The dates shown are the last valid ones. Remove one of the links to recover.
schedule.unknownTask: This task no longer exists. Reload the page.
schedule.undoHint: Undo the last change — Ctrl+Z. It is written to the database, not just to the screen.
schedule.redoHint: Redo the change just undone — Ctrl+Y.
schedule.cannotReparent: A task can only be moved within its own group. To change its parent, use the task form.
schedule.formIdentity: {type}. The type governs which fields have meaning and is not changed here.
schedule.milestoneZero: A milestone has no duration by construction.
schedule.startAnchorHint: Pins the start. Leave empty to let the task follow its predecessors or the project start.
schedule.endHint: Always start + duration. Never entered: it is a result.
schedule.progressHint: Percent complete, entered by hand. It draws the dark band inside the bar, and a task past its end date with less than 100% shows as late.
schedule.writeFailed: The database refused the write. Your change was rolled back.
schedule.deleteTaskHint: Archives the task and its children. It is not erased — Ctrl+Z brings it back, and the change log keeps the trace.
schedule.codeRace: Two tasks were created at the same instant. Try again.
schedule.constraintHint: Holds the task back until this date, whatever else would allow it to start earlier.
schedule.constraintHintLinked: This is how you hold a linked task back. Unlike a start date, a constraint only ever PUSHES — the task starts at the later of this date and its predecessor's end, so the link stays true.

gantt.title: Gantt
gantt.intro: Rendered in-house as SVG, with no dependency (see docs/GANTT_ARBITRAGE.md).
gantt.noTasks: No task to display for this scenario.
gantt.showAllColumnsHint: Show owner, predecessors, site and progress. The grid widens, so the diagram narrows.
gantt.showFewerColumnsHint: Keep only activity, duration and dates, to give the diagram room.
gantt.showNamesHint: Write each task name next to its bar. Useful for a screenshot; noisy on a dense plan.

deliverables.title: Deliverables
deliverables.intro: Consultant reports and contractor deliverables. Lateness is derived at read time, never stored: a stored flag would be wrong the day after it was computed.
deliverables.wasLateNote: Submitted after the contractual date. The fact stays visible once the deliverable is in.
deliverables.lateCount: {count} deliverable(s) past their contractual date and not submitted.
deliverables.emptyNote: The register is empty because no deliverable appears in the source documents. It fills as the PIU and the technical assistance record what they receive (brief §3): consultants and contractors are not users of this platform.
deliverables.byContractIntro: What is open, what is late, and what comes next for each of the 9 procedures.
deliverables.issuerHint: Consultant or contractor, in plain text: they are not users of this platform (brief §3).
deliverables.markSubmittedHint: Record today as the submission date and move the status to submitted.
deliverables.visaHint: Record that you validated this deliverable. Declarative, not a signature.
deliverables.error_noOrigin: A deliverable must be attached to a contract or a lot.

org.title: Org chart
org.intro: The 11 PIU functions plus the platform administrator, the technical assistance and the AFD task team. The sources contain no unit above the posts themselves, so this is a tree of posts (GAPS 28).
org.unfilledNote: Posts with no holder are normal at this stage: accounts are opened one by one by the administrator (see docs/ADMIN.md). The 14 on-site representatives in particular have no named assignment in any source (GAPS 29).

library.title: Library
library.intro: Files live in Cloudflare R2, never in Postgres. Uploads go straight from the browser to R2 — they never pass through a server function (brief §4).
library.noTagNote: A document with no tag is visible to every active MG2030 user (brief §7).
library.emptyFolder: No document in this folder yet
library.emptyNote: The library is empty because nothing has been uploaded yet. The folder tree comes from seed/folder_tree.csv and is a proposal, not project data.
library.treeIsProposal: This tree is a proposal (seed/folder_tree.csv). Administrators can reorganise it freely.
library.r2NotConfigured: Cloudflare R2 is not configured: the R2_* variables are missing from the environment. Browsing works, uploading does not. See .env.example.
library.error_forbidden: You do not have permission to upload documents.
library.error_r2_not_configured: Cloudflare R2 is not configured on this environment.
library.error_size_out_of_range: File is empty or larger than 5 GB.
library.error_mime_type_blocked: This file type is not accepted in the library.
library.error_folder_not_found: That folder does not exist, or you cannot access it.
library.error_upload_failed: The transfer to storage failed. Nothing was recorded.
library.error_orphan: The file reached storage but could not be recorded. Object key: {key} — pass it to an administrator so the orphan can be cleaned up.
library.error_not_found: This document does not exist, or you cannot access it.
library.error_downloadFailed: The download link could not be issued.
library.viewHint: Open in a new tab. PDFs and images display inline; other types download.

notifications.title: Notifications
notifications.intro: Applicative only — no email is sent in version 1 (brief §7). Event notifications come from triggers; state ones (lateness, upcoming deadlines) from the periodic evaluation, because nobody performs the act of missing a deadline.
notifications.emptyNote: Nothing yet, and that is expected: no task carries an owner and no deliverable is recorded, so lateness notifications have no recipient (GAPS 8). They will appear once the PIU assigns tasks. The periodic evaluation also needs SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY and CRON_SECRET (GAPS 54).

noObjections.title: AFD no-objections
noObjections.intro: Nothing gets signed without an AFD no-objection, which makes this the main source of procurement delay. Lateness is measured against the duration the schedule allows for the task the request carries — never against an invented standard turnaround.
noObjections.subject: Subject
noObjections.taskHint: Without a linked task there is no allowed duration, so no lateness can be stated — only elapsed time.
noObjections.taskLinked: The schedule allows {days} days for this task. Beyond that the request shows as overdue.
noObjections.taskSourceNote: {count} schedule tasks are AFD no-objections. Linking a request to one of them is what turns elapsed time into a verdict.
noObjections.sentDateHint: Leave empty to keep the request as a draft. Filling it marks the request as sent.
noObjections.noReferenceTooltip: No linked task, so no allowed duration: elapsed time only, no verdict.
noObjections.markSentHint: Record today as the send date. Nothing can be counted before it.
noObjections.cancelHint: A withdrawn request is kept, not erased: AFD holds its own trace of it.
noObjections.emptyNote: Nothing yet, and that is expected: the source documents record no no-objection request (GAPS 8). The schedule already carries the AFD steps as tasks — TV.2.3, SC.2.4 and the negotiation steps. Record a request against one of them and the delay becomes measurable.
noObjections.confirmDelete: Delete the request « {subject} »? Withdrawing is usually the right move — it keeps the trace.
noObjections.error_noTarget: A request must be attached to a contract, a lot or a task.

procurement.title: Procurement templates
procurement.intro: Creating a contract instantiates a template and generates its tasks (brief §7). No template is project data: the sources contain none. The two sequences offered have their durations READ OFF the real chains of the schedule — C-TV-DD for consultant selection, TV.3.1 for the works tender — not estimated. Review each one before activating it: a duration that was observed is still not a duration that was agreed.
procurement.confirmDeleteTemplate: Delete template {code}? Tasks already generated from it are kept — only the template goes.
procurement.seedObservedHint: Creates the two sequences read off the real schedule — consultant selection and works tender — INACTIVE, so they are not mistaken for validated data.
procurement.emptyNote: This is expected: the source documents contain no procurement template (GAPS 10). Start from the observed sequences — their durations are read off the real chains of C-TV-DD and TV.3.1, not estimated — then review each one before activating.
procurement.stepHint: Steps chain finish-to-start. A step anchored on a contract milestone takes that date instead: the procurement plan is the contractual document, and the template must not drift from it. A notice publication anchors the START of a step; a bid opening, a signature and a completion anchor its END, because those are terminal events. A step marked AFD also creates a draft no-objection request.
procurement.generateIntro: Preview first, apply second. Nothing is written until you apply.
procurement.previewSummary: {create} tasks to create, {skip} skipped, {nons} no-objection requests.
procurement.noAnchorWarning: This contract carries no milestone date, so the dates below start from today. They are a placeholder, not a forecast: fill in at least the notice publication or bid opening date on the contract before relying on them.
procurement.contractHasTasks: This contract already carries {count} tasks. Existing WBS codes will be skipped, not overwritten.
procurement.anchorsIntro: These dates drive the generated schedule. A contract with none produces placeholder dates.
procurement.error_emptyIdentity: A code and a name are required.
procurement.error_invalidStepNo: Step number must be a positive whole number.
procurement.error_invalidDuration: Duration must be a whole number of days, zero or more.
procurement.error_templateHasNoStep: This template has no step: there is nothing to generate.
procurement.conflictTooltip: The contract date makes this step start before the previous one ends. The contract date wins — it is the contractual document — but the two documents disagree here (GAPS 13).
procurement.slackTooltip: The contract date leaves idle time after the previous step ends.
procurement.conflictWarning: {count} steps start before their predecessor ends, because the procurement plan and the chained durations disagree (GAPS 13). The contract dates win. Check them before applying — this is a real divergence between two source documents, not a calculation error.
procurement.isNoObjectionLabel: This step is an AFD no-objection
procurement.conflictWarningOne: One step starts before its predecessor ends, because the procurement plan and the chained durations disagree (GAPS 13). The contract date wins. Check it before applying — this is a real divergence between two source documents, not a calculation error.

map.title: Site map
map.intro: The 14 sites, located from the mapping supplied on 25/08/2026 (GAPS 71). Gold marks the Athletes’ Village, blue the training venue halls.
map.missingCoordinates: {count} sites have no coordinates and do not appear on the map.
map.sourceNote: Map data © OpenStreetMap contributors. Coordinates read off Carte Pristina / All locs.pdf, not surveyed on site — treat placement as approximate.
